sentences.text: This dinosaur featured a very long beak that reached 70% of the total skull length.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes an almost complete skeleton with preserved feather remains.
The fossil was discovered near Lingyuan in the Aptian-aged Jiufotang Formation.
The species Juehuaornis zhangi was named and described in 2015 by Wang Ren-fe, Wang Yan, and Hu Dongyu.
The genus name combines the name of Juehua Island, known as "Chrysanthemum Island" off Liaoning, with the Greek word for bird.
The specific name zhangi honors the curator Zhang Dayong.
Juehuaornis was classified within the Ornithuromorpha in 2015.
Juehuaornis was an extinct ornithuromorph dinosaur that lived in present-day China during the Early Cretaceous.
Fossils of this animal date from the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
It is debated whether Juehuaornis should be considered the same genus as Changzuiornis and Dingavis, which would grant Juehuaornis priority.
